correctness.rationale: Markushevich–Moreau exhaustive stabilizer data: 21 involutions with four fixed elliptic components each, of which one is a C4 axis; remaining distinct translates contribute 63 generic C2 curves. There are 28 cyclic C3 fixed curves and 21 cyclic C4 fixed curves, giving 112. Setwise normalizers of curve components D8,S3,D8 produce H-orbit sizes 21,28,21 and hence 3+1+1 irreducible image curves. The tangent H action lies in SL3(C), so no pseudoreflections; nonfree locus equals singular preimage. Transverse eigenvalues of C2,C3,C4 give cyclic quotient uv=w^n and ADE A1,A2,A3. Source classifies 48 isolated order-7 fixed points split into two H-orbits of 24 yielding two isolated 1/7(1,2,4) points. Independently recomputed orbit arithmetic and local eigenvalue invariants; finite script verifies arithmetic but exhaustiveness rests on actual primary-source fixed-locus classification.
residual_risks: Generic transverse ADE labels do not extend to special intersections.
Claims reduced singular locus, not all local schemes or crepant resolution.

value.rationale: The reduced singular locus and ADE basket are natural global invariants of the canonical Klein-Jacobian Calabi–Yau orbifold and key inputs to resolution and stringy geometry. The finite orbit decomposition distinguishes Y from the much smoother reflection quotient X and is more than a gratuitous arithmetic restatement of a subgroup table.
residual_risks: Input fixed-locus/stabilizer data are from prior publication, not newly derived.

final_claim: For Y=Jac(Klein quartic)/PSL(2,7) over C, reduced singular locus consists of exactly five curves (generic transverse types three A1, one A2 and one A3) and two isolated cyclic 1/7(1,2,4) points. Preimage nonfree locus consists of 112 elliptic curves in three+one+one H-orbits.
limitations: Generic ADE singularity along curves, not singularity model at every special point.
Relies on completeness of original H fixed-locus classification, not a standalone independent enumeration of Jacobian fixed points.
